analysis: ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift head:46-52 adds deferred watchdog rearming on both successful and throwing relaunches. UpdateCommand.swift head:162-169 wraps stop/restart with that helper after candidate preparation; rearming now also occurs on stop/restart failure, before session release and pending-candidate cancellation. Successful-path ordering remains unchanged. Existing config selection, auto-restart policy and suppressed watchdog-operation errors at ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift:20-34 are unchanged. ServiceDrainRearmTests.swift:22-47 tests callback invocation, config forwarding and error propagation, but not actual watchdog/launchd interactions. No supported security regression appears in the supplied source. Relevant lifecycle concerns are T-043/TB-003 (recovery authority and availability), T-053/A-008 (stop/logout must not resurrect credential custody), and T-047 (fan-control lifecycle). No direct encryption, attestation, billing, prompt exposure or T-041 cache-policy changes are visible. Integration must inspect ServiceDrain.prepare/stopDrainedProvider, LaunchAgent.restartAfterDrain, WatchdogAgent and SelfUpdater candidate/lease handling: specifically whether a watchdog armed before the failure catch releases the session can act before pending-candidate cancellation, and whether failed stop or concurrent logout remains fenced. Those implementations and other callers were not supplied; unit tests alone do not resolve those interactions.
